🇲🇽📊 <u>BBVA CUTS MEXICO 2026 GDP TO 1.2% — THE DRAG IS MADE IN WASHINGTON</u>

BBVA cut its 2026 Mexico growth forecast to 1.2% (from 1.8%), citing a 6.5% drop in fixed investment in machinery and equipment through March under Trump's tariff uncertainty. It still sees the World Cup adding ~0.3% to GDP this quarter and a rebound to 1.8% in 2027 as energy mixed-contracts advance and trade tension eases. The brake is external — not internal.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>WORLD CUP SECURITY, ON MEXICO'S TERMS — NOT WASHINGTON'S</u>

Mexican Special Forces from Semar and Sedena coordinated 2026 World Cup security with US and Canadian commands in Tampa, May 16–22. Semar was explicit: the collaboration runs "bajo los principios de reciprocidad, responsabilidad compartida, confianza mutua y respeto a la soberanía." Shared security, synchronized training — not occupation. That's the line between cooperation and the unilateral intervention Trump keeps floating.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>THE STATE IS INVESTIGATING CRIME'S GRIP ON MEXICO'S MINES — AND WHO BENEFITS</u>

Sheinbaum confirmed the government is investigating organized crime's infiltration of the mining sector: criminal cells hired to break up union meetings, violate labor rights, and extort miners. The Sindicato Nacional Minero names a pattern across Plata Panamericana (Zacatecas), Americas Gold & Silver (Sinaloa) and Torex Gold (Guerrero) — echoing the Camino Rojo case where a "known drug trafficker" was contracted to threaten workers at gunpoint. The companies, many foreign, let crime do their union-busting.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO'S SUPREME COURT AFFIRMS INDIGENOUS SELF-GOVERNMENT</u>

The SCJN just upheld Indigenous peoples' right to self-determination: the Zapotec community of San Juan Atepec can enforce its own internal norms and resolve disputes through its own procedures. "Los pueblos y comunidades indígenas tienen derecho a la libre determinación" — so long as human rights are respected. Constitutional autonomy, recognized by the highest court, five centuries after the conquest tried to erase it.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>SHEINBAUM TO THE TEACHERS: DIALOGUE STAYS OPEN, THE OLD CORRUPT MODEL DOESN'T</u>

Sheinbaum keeps the door open to the CNTE, but rules out a return to the model where union bosses and government carved up decisions behind closed doors — "se presta a corrupción." She signed an accord with CNTE Section 7 of Chiapas and sent resources straight to Oaxaca's schools, not to union leadership. "No puedes hablar de democracia sindical y querer seguir siendo representante."

🚨🇲🇽 <u>NO IMSS, NO EXPORTS: MEXICO TIES FARMWORKERS' RIGHTS TO AGRIBUSINESS PROFITS</u>

Mexico just told its export agribusiness in San Quintín, Baja California: register every jornalero with IMSS social security within six months — or lose the certificate you need to export. Sheinbaum's Plan de Justicia now binds the right to export to the right to social security for workers who labor up to 18 hours a day "a destajo." She promised to come back in six months to verify. 36,000 families also get 40,000 pesos for housing.

🇲🇽🏭 MEXICO COULD CAPTURE $18 BILLION IN DATA-CENTER INVESTMENT BY 2030

Nearshoring is going digital: Mexico stands to attract up to $18 billion in data centers over five years and add 1.5 GW of capacity — a sector that could contribute as much as 5% of GDP, with Querétaro alone hosting 22 announced projects. The bottleneck is electricity, and the state is moving to meet it: the CFE has committed $23.4 billion through 2030 to expand generation, transmission and distribution.

🇲🇽🏘️ 1.44 BILLION PESOS FOR 36,000 FAMILIES IN SAN QUINTÍN

President Sheinbaum announced 40,000 pesos for each of 36,000 families in San Quintín, Baja California to improve their homes — alongside land-title regularization, electricity and potable water for residents long stranded on irregularly sold ejido land. "Now 36,000 families will each be given 40,000 pesos to improve their housing conditions," she said, pledging to return in six months to check on progress.

🔥🇲🇽 THE CONSTRUCTION GIANT BEHIND XÓCHITL GÁLVEZ

Morena's Mario Delgado and Víctor Hugo Romero say opposition figure Xóchitl Gálvez runs her political operation out of offices owned by Grupo Marhnos — rent-free — the same firm that built seven hospitals between 2011 and 2015 amid inflated-cost and corruption claims. Their example: the Ticul hospital in Yucatán billed nearly 5 billion pesos against a real budget of 500 million. "That constitutes influence peddling and corruption," Delgado said.

🚨🇲🇽 US INTERCEPTS 43,000 ROUNDS HEADED TO MEXICO — THE GUNS GO ONE WAY

US Customs seized more than 43,000 cartridges bound for Mexico in a single day at Arizona's Mariposa crossing: two vehicles carrying 15,000 and 28,000 rounds of 7.62×39 — AK-47 ammunition. Even Trump's own ambassador, Ronald Johnson, is now confirming what Mexico has said for years: the firepower arming the cartels is American-made and flows south.
